newsitem.title: FRANCE: Fr. Telecom shareholders funds 62 bln ffr.
newsitem.headline: Fr. Telecom shareholders funds 62 bln ffr.

text.p: The shareholders funds of France Telecom, due to be partially privatised in the spring, have been set at 62 billion francs for 1996.
Due to a legal reserve of 2.5 billion and a nominal share capital of 25 billion, the share premium would be 34.5 billion francs.
The "net situation" -- the balance sheet total minus debts and provisions -- at the start of 1996 was put at 72.43 billion francs.
This is made up of 62 billion in own assets, 9.86 billion in reserves and 568 million in investment grants.

The figures, published in the Official Bulletin, were drawn up in order "to give France Telecom SA a set of accounts for 1996 that will be comparable with the coming years, so that analysts can make their forecasts," a Finance Ministry official said.
The total net assets of France Telecom's activities needed for the "public service" of telecommunications are valued at 1.1 billion francs.
The provisions for exceptional charges, such as the one-off pension payment to the state, has been set at 24.7 billion francs.
France Telecom SA has one billion shares of 25 francs each.
The Finance Ministry official said that the shareholders funds at the end of 1996, as well as those of the start of 1997, would not be known until after the 1996 company results were finalised.
